public_rationale: The announcements document the factual core: Google included Gemini and gave a Business Standard example costing $2 more per user per month; Microsoft bundled Copilot and raised consumer subscription prices. But Microsoft offered eligible existing subscribers non-AI alternatives, and Google's example does not establish a uniform increase. The broader assertion that affected customers generally did not want the features remains unverified. The complete claim therefore cannot receive an unqualified outcome.
limitations: The pricing records establish individual components under separate company and reporting scopes.
Some existing customers faced changes at renewal rather than immediately.
Non-AI alternatives qualify compulsory bundling but do not establish how easy customers found them to access.
The conclusion does not treat lack of customer-demand evidence as proof that customers wanted AI.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Google and Microsoft are now forcing generative AI features onto customers: Google by raising Google Workspace prices for business users by $2 per user per month along with AI features they don't want, and Microsoft by raising consumer Office subscription prices, justified by adding Copilot AI features customers really don't want.
conditions: Google: business users of Google Workspace

statement.excerpt: Both Google and Microsoft are now forcing generative AI features onto customers, with Google grifting business users by increasing the cost of Google Workspace by $2-per-user-per-month along with AI features they don't want, and Microsoft raising the price of consumer Office subscriptions, justifying the move by adding Copilot AI features that, again, customers really don't want.

from_speaker: now forcing generative AI features onto customers
our_interpretation: Now refers to the subscription changes announced in January 2025 by the post date, including changes scheduled to apply at renewal.
Treat forcing as moving customers into an AI-inclusive paid bundle by default without their choosing an AI add-on. Whether comparable non-AI plans remained available is a material qualification.
Treat customers don't want the features as a general demand claim about the affected subscriber populations, not a claim that literally no customer wants AI.
The Google amount must be checked by plan and billing arrangement. A matching example does not establish a uniform increase for all Workspace business users.
The post links press reporting, so the contract records estimate as its reporting basis. Company announcements are kept under their own company_reported basis.
The claim combines two companies and different subscription units. Individual-company pricing evidence is component context, not an interchangeable measurement of the combined scope.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes the stated Google price increase for the relevant plans, a Microsoft consumer-subscription increase tied to Copilot, default AI bundling, and representative evidence that affected customers generally did not want the bundled features.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence disproves a stated pricing or bundling component, or representative evidence shows affected customers generally wanted the features. Accessible comparable non-AI plans would materially qualify a compulsory-bundling reading.

evidence.explanation: The announcement documents Copilot bundling and a $3 monthly US price increase, with existing subscribers affected at renewal. It also describes eligible subscribers' non-Copilot options, qualifying a claim of unavoidable bundling.

evidence.explanation: The report corroborates Microsoft's alternatives and clarifies their pricing and restriction to existing subscribers. This is material counterevidence to an absolute reading of forcing, without showing that customers generally wanted Copilot.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Contemporaneous plan-level terms and representative research measuring demand for the bundled features among the affected Google business and Microsoft consumer subscribers, with the meaning of forcing fixed explicitly.
